read_oracle_feasibility.candidate: Non-interference (semantic): the answer must not change when state outside the declared footprint changes
read_oracle_feasibility.can_observe: any read outside the declared footprint that influences the answer, at row granularity (another graph's rows with the same ids, other keys/labels/predicates/prefixes in the same graph, stores the action does not declare, other tenants' ledger history)
read_oracle_feasibility.cannot_observe: a read outside the footprint whose value never reaches the answer (it costs time, not correctness); perturbations not tried (the set per action is listed in per_module)

method: Oracle A, per read action: base state from lib.reset() (product's own EraseAll + PurgeAll) on a fresh connection, the action run on a fresh engine; run twice (stable answer required); for each perturbation OUTSIDE the declared footprint, base + perturbation, run again; a changed answer (canonical form: lists sorted, floats to 10 digits; an order-only change is recorded separately) is a read outside the declared footprint. Where given, a perturbation INSIDE the footprint must change the answer (sensitivity); where it does not, the cell says so. Outside perturbations used: the same ids (and one more) with other labels, properties, edges, temporal edges or vectors in every other graph (default graph and stg1/stg2); other ids/labels/keys in the same graph (including LIKE wildcard characters in ids and keys); another predicate in the same graph; other tenants' ledger commits; the tenant's ids written directly in a named graph; a scratch global ^IVGAuditDRdSnap (removed after each variant). Oracle B (table level) as in the feasibility table.
